title: Cabin Window Pane Protective Coating and Intercostal Reinforcement

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Cabin Window Assembly

abstract: Cancelled change that would have added a sacrificial coating to the cabin window pane outer face and reinforced the intercostal, dropped when the coating failed its optical acceptance and the underlying crazing was attributed to a cleaning agent.

sections.reason: Operators were replacing cabin window panes for outer face crazing at roughly three times the rate assumed for spares provisioning, and two operators asked for either a more durable pane or a wider rework allowance. The proposal was to apply a sacrificial coating at build, which could be renewed in the shop, and to reinforce the intercostal so that the coating renewal could be done without removing the surrounding structure.
sections.description: The proposed change applied a two-part sacrificial coating to the pane outer face and replaced the intercostal with a reinforced item, together with a revised plate at the frame joint and current-standard collars at the fastener positions. During qualification the coating passed the abrasion and thermal cycling requirements but failed the optical distortion acceptance at the pane edge on two of six samples, and no reformulation was available inside the programme window. In parallel a field investigation attributed the crazing rate to a ramp cleaning agent used at four stations, which is outside the aircraft standard.
sections.effects: None, since the change was cancelled before any embodiment. Provisioning for the reinforced intercostal was released and then withdrawn, and no aircraft carries any part of this modification. Operators were issued with the cleaning agent finding as a service information item and with the interim protective film already available for other fleets.
sections.embodiment_note: Cancelled at the design review in June 2025. No production cut-in, no bulletin and no spares. Any future attempt would restart from the coating qualification.
